1.title: Troubleshooting and Observability
1.text: Welcome to Module fourteen: Troubleshooting and Observability. It covers the exam area Domain four: Troubleshooting and Optimization. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. Debug application code and service integration issues (four point one.one). Interpret metrics, logs and traces (four point one.two). Query logs (four point one.three). Troubleshoot deployment failures with output logs (four point one.four). Use A W S A I tools to analyze errors (four point one.five). Implement effective logging, custom metrics, notification alerts, tracing and health monitoring (four point two.one to four point two.five). Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Domain four: Troubleshooting and Optimization (twenty-two percent). Exam format: fifty scored questions, multiple choice and multiple response; a score of seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official A W S Developer Associate (D V A-C three) exam guide.

1.title: The three pillars
1.text: The three pillars. The figure shows this: Logs, metrics and traces: three views of the same system.

1.title: The three pillars, continued
1.text: The three pillars. Logs. Service: Amazon Cloud Watch Logs. Answers: What happened? Metrics. Service: Amazon Cloud Watch metrics and alarms. Answers: How is it performing? Traces. Service: A W S X-Ray. Answers: Where is the time or the failure across services? A W S Cloud Trail records A P I calls (who did what), a different job: auditing.

1.title: CloudWatch Logs
1.text: Cloud Watch Logs. Log group or log stream. A group per application; a stream per source (for example per Lambda instance). Retention. Set it; default is never expire. Logs Insights. Query language to search and aggregate logs. Metric filter. Turn log patterns into a metric (for example, count error ). Structured logging. Log Jason with fields (request I D, user, action) so queries are easy. Exam tip: "Find the slowest requests in the logs" equals Cloud Watch Logs Insights. "Alarm on the number of errors in logs" equals metric filter plus alarm.

1.title: Metrics, alarms and notifications
1.text: Metrics, alarms and notifications. Custom metrics. Your code emits values with Put Metric Data or Embedded Metric Format (E M F) logs. Alarm. Watches a metric and changes state; can notify through S N S or trigger actions. Notifications. S N S email or messages for quota limits or deployment completions (via Event Bridge rules). Health checks. Load balancer target health checks; container liveness and readiness probes (E K S).

1.title: Tracing with AWS X-Ray
1.text: Tracing with A W S X-Ray. Trace. The path of one request through services. Segment or subsegment. A unit of work in a service; subsegments for downstream calls. Annotations. Indexed key-value pairs you can filter and search by. Metadata. Extra data not indexed. Sampling. Trace a fraction of requests to control cost. Enable. Turn on active tracing for Lambda or A P I Gateway; use the X-Ray S D K or daemon elsewhere. Exam tip: Annotations are searchable; metadata is not. "Find which downstream call is slow" equals X-Ray service map and traces.

1.title: Root cause analysis
1.text: Root cause analysis. H T T P four x x. Client request problem: validation, auth, throttling (four hundred twenty-nine). H T T P five x x or five hundred two or five hundred four. Backend error, bad response, or timeout (five hundred four gateway timeout). Lambda timeout. Raise timeout or optimize; check downstream latency. Lambda throttled. Concurrency limit reached. Deployment failure. Read Cloud Formation stack events and Code Deploy or Code Build output logs. Access denied. Check the role policy, resource policy and K M S key policy. A W S A I tools can analyze errors and suggest fixes; verify the suggestion before applying it. Exam tip: A five x x points to the backend, a four x x to the request, a five hundred four to a timeout. Read the status code before choosing the fix.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A team wants to know which downstream service adds the most latency to a request. What should they use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: A W S X-Ray traces. X-Ray shows the path and timing of a request across services.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A team wants an alarm when the word "error" appears more than ten times a minute in logs. What should they create? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A metric filter and a Cloud Watch alarm. A metric filter turns log patterns into a metric to alarm on.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Which X-Ray feature lets a developer search traces by customer I D? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Annotations. Annotations are indexed and searchable.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Logs are unstructured text and hard to query. What is the best improvement? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Structured Jason logging with consistent fields. Structured logs are easy to filter and aggregate.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A Cloud Formation deployment failed. Where should the developer look first? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Stack events. Stack events show which resource failed and why.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A function returns H T T P five hundred four through A P I Gateway. What is the likely cause? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: The backend took longer than the integration timeout. five hundred four means a gateway timeout from a slow backend.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Name the three pillars of observability. Answer: Logs, metrics and traces. Question two. Which service records A P I activity? Answer: A W S Cloud Trail. Question three. What does Logs Insights do? Answer: Queries and aggregates Cloud Watch Logs.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is the difference between X-Ray annotations and metadata? Answer: Annotations are indexed and searchable; metadata is not. Question five. What emits custom metrics from code? Answer: Put Metric Data or Embedded Metric Format logs. Question six. What does H T T P four hundred twenty-nine mean? Answer: Too many requests (throttling); retry with backoff.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Pillars: logs (Cloud Watch Logs), metrics (Cloud Watch), traces (X-Ray); Cloud Trail audits. Logs: groups and streams, retention, Insights, metric filters, structured Jason. X-Ray: traces, segments, annotations (searchable), metadata, sampling. Alerts: alarms, S N S, Event Bridge, health checks. Errors: four x x client, five x x backend, five hundred four timeout, four hundred twenty-nine throttle.
